ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diameter $AB=6$ of circle $\odot O$, with chord $CD$ of $\odot O$ perpendicular to $AB$ at point $P$, and $BP:AP=1:5$, what is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the diameter $AB$ of the circle $\odot O$ equals 6,\\
it follows that $OB=\frac{1}{2}AB=3$,\\
since the ratio $BP:AP=1:5$,\\
we have $BP=\frac{1}{6}AB=\frac{1}{6} \times 6=1$,\\
thus $OP=OB-BP=3-1=2$,\\
by joining $OC$,\\
and since $CD\perp AB$,\\
it implies $CD=2PC$, and $\angle OPC=90^\circ$,\\
therefore, $PC=\sqrt{OC^{2}-OP^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
resulting in $CD=2PC=2\sqrt{5}$.\\
Hence, the length of $CD$ is $\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$.

First read the diagram: AB is the horizontal diameter of the circle, O is its center on AB, and the vertical chord CD meets AB at P to the right of O; C and D are symmetric above and below AB.
